03

Living communities and further study

BIA reports that recognition enacted in December 2025 was formalized in the federal tribal list in 2026. Older summaries of Lumbee recognition need updating.

Read the sources [2] Bureau of Indian Affairs

04

Reconstructing Baltimore Lumbee history through memories and archives

In her 2019 essay, Ashley Minner explains how elders’ recollections led her to reconstruct East Baltimore’s Lumbee history through institutional archives. She describes working with newspaper clippings, early community-center newsletters, historical maps and city directories. Her stated aim includes helping younger Lumbee generations recognize the depth of that history. This is Minner’s account of her research, not an Atlas inspection of the underlying collections or a report of completed outcomes.

Read the sources [3] University of Maryland, Baltimore County; republication of The Conversation essay

05

A published chronology of the Baltimore American Indian Center

Ashley Minner Jones’s Baltimore Heritage item states that the American Indian Study Center became the Baltimore American Indian Center in 1980. It reports that the Baltimore American Indian Center Heritage Museum opened in 2011. This supplies limited institutional chronology alongside the Baltimore Lumbee reading route, without treating the institutions as exclusively Lumbee or verifying present services.

Read the sources [4] Explore Baltimore Heritage / Baltimore Heritage

What needs further research

  • Minner’s essay adds one attributed Baltimore Lumbee research perspective. The Atlas has not inspected its underlying oral or archival materials; further community-led comparison and the two older unreviewed references remain unfinished. This does not verify present property, legal status, ancestry or complete community history.
  • This supporting chronology does not inspect the Center’s underlying institutional records or supply a full history, present-service account or media clearance. Broader community-directed comparison remains unfinished; the earlier research-method account keeps its separate scope and date.

A Quest to Reconstruct Baltimore’s American Indian ‘Reservation’ — selected research account ↗

Publication: UMBC copy published April 23, 2019; first publication of the underlying essay unestablished

Ashley Minner describes reconstructing East Baltimore’s Lumbee history by combining elders’ memories with newspapers and institutional archives. Her account follows the research trail through newsletters, historical maps and city directories. These are her reported methods; the Atlas has not inspected the underlying records.

Baltimore American Indian Center — selected institutional chronology ↗

Publication: Published November 2, 2023; last updated April 17, 2026 (displayed item dates)

Ashley Minner Jones’s item dates the Center’s name change to 1980 and the museum’s opening to 2011. These selected statements add published institutional chronology alongside the Baltimore Lumbee reading route. They do not independently verify institutional records, make the institutions exclusively Lumbee, establish present services or add substantive community-history credit.
